mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a recession (UNRATE < 3% at trigger).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5.5% for two consecutive months signals a late-cycle labor market overheating, which increases wage pressures and reduces corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or UNRATE rises above 5.5% within one month after trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or GDP growth turns positive within the next quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals a manufacturing slowdown, which depresses earnings expectations and causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or INDPRO re-crosses above its moving average within two months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and core CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 2% for two consecutive months signals a dual monetary and inflationary shock, which increases real discount rates and erodes real corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL > 2% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or inflation falls below 2% within one month after trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months, combined with a stable unemployment rate (UNRATE), signals a tightening labor market without overt wage inflation, which boosts consumer spending and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month moving average for 3 consecutive months AND UNRATE stable (±0.1%)
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or UNRATE rises by >0.3% within one month after trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in housing starts (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals a recovery in residential investment, which boosts construction-related equities and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month moving average for 5 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or HOUST falls below its moving average within two months after trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real personal savings (RSAFS) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months, coupled with stable consumer spending (implied by GDPC1 not falling), suggests increased consumption financed by debt, which can temporarily support equities but ultimately raises default risk and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 12-month moving average for 4 consecutive months AND GDPC1 stable (±0.5% q/q)
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or RSAFS rebounds above its moving average within the next quarter.
